name: Superoxide dismutase
lead: Superoxide dismutase (SOD) is a family of metalloenzymes that convert the superoxide radical into oxygen and hydrogen peroxide and is regarded as a first line of antioxidant defense in most oxygen-using organisms. [2] The enzymatic activity was identified in 1969 by James McCord and Irwin Fridovich in a copper protein from red blood cells. [1]

In skincare, SOD is added to products marketed as antioxidant or anti-photoaging. No published trial of topical SOD for cosmetic anti-aging was found. Registered human trials of SOD have mostly concerned radiation-related skin injury and oral supplements. [3]
infobox: Cosmetic ingredient; not an approved anti-aging drug

paras: Mammals have three main isoforms: SOD1 in the cytosol, SOD2 in mitochondria and SOD3 outside cells. [2] Variants of the SOD1 gene are associated with familial amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. [7]
SOD sits within a wider literature on oxidative stress in conditions such as diabetes complications and cancer. [9][10]

SOD is promoted as one ingredient in antioxidant serums and creams and in oral supplements sold for skin. Community discussion of it is sparse compared with ingredients such as vitamin C or retinoids.

Registered human trials involving SOD include a completed trial of oral SOD (GliSODin) for melasma severity in 40 participants, a completed study of topical SOD for radiation-induced fibrosis in head and neck cancer patients (n=74), and a recruiting phase 2 trial of an SOD skin spray for radiation dermatitis. [4][3][5] Other registrations involve diabetic neuropathy, male infertility and esophagitis during radiation. [6][8][11] Results are not summarized here, and none of these tested SOD for cosmetic anti-aging in healthy skin.

timeline.event: McCord and Fridovich report the enzymic function of erythrocuprein as superoxide dismutase. [1]

card.summary: An antioxidant enzyme added to anti-aging products; biologically central, but cosmetic evidence is essentially unstudied.
card.note: Registered trials concern radiation skin injury and oral supplements, not cosmetic anti-aging.

quick.overview:
Superoxide dismutase is a naturally occurring enzyme family that neutralizes the superoxide radical. It is added to some topical products and oral supplements marketed for antioxidant skin protection.

No published trial of topical SOD for cosmetic anti-aging was found; registered human trials concern mostly radiation skin injury and oral supplements.
quick.mechanism: SOD converts superoxide into oxygen and hydrogen peroxide. Humans have cytosolic (SOD1), mitochondrial (SOD2) and extracellular (SOD3) forms.
quick.risks: No cosmetic-specific safety data were found. Wikipedia notes that bovine-derived SOD drugs were withdrawn in several European countries over prion concerns.
